newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie dlr finds upside capped,tests lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie dlr finds upside capped,tests lower.

text.p: AUS$ S/Term range *Support *Restnce *RSI-14 *MA-10 *MA-20
*Offshore range roughly US$0.7380/7432
*Aussie dollar drops half a cent in offshore trade to be testing key support at US$0.7380 in early local trade.
*Dollar tries downside after solid resistance above US0.7430 prevents it from retesting last week's highs of US$0.7483.
*Market waiting on RBA quarterly report on the economy and U.S. FOMC meeting later today.
The Australian dollar had dropped half a cent in overnight trade to its lowest level in one week and was testing the key support level of US$0.7380 in early local trade.

Traders said there was good exporter demand that was expected to provide solid support to the dollar, which made the move lower after running into difficulty during European trading when it tested US$0.7430.
By 8.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7381/86, down from US$0.7423/28 late on Monday.

Over the first four days of last week, the dollar rallied strongly from a two year low of US$0.7295 to reach a high of US$0.7483 on Thursday. Since then, the dollar has set lower peaks each day, and has found willing sellers on any rally.
An overnight fall in the gold price also weighed on the dollar, and it took little comfort from the 108.70 point recovery in the Dow Jones stock index after Friday's fall.

If support at US$0.7380 and then US$0.7350 was breached, it was possible the unit could test the low US$0.73 area, although traders said there was little to suggest the US$0.73/75 range, held since early July, was currently under any serious threat.

The overnight fall in the dollar started in European trading, where after an early move to US$0.7430, the dollar ran into selling that took it to support at US$0.7400/05. It showed some signs of holding there until U.S. sellers entered in New York trading and took it to its lows.
It was above US$0.7380 that local buyers entered when the dollar dipped on Friday, and the dollar had steadied at this level in early trade.
The market is now waiting on the release of the Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly report on the economy and the U.S. FOMC meeting later today.

The RBA report is expected to replay some of the themes of governor Macfarlane's sppech last week -- there is some excess capacity in the economy that could see it grow above 4.5 percent in coming years, but inflation is not a constraint on growth.

While a repeat of this sort of bullish growth outlook may dent the dollar as it would be seen as maintaining an easing bias in rates, Macfarlane also said he did not consider monetary policy settings restrictive.
The FOMC meets later today, with the outcome of the meeting known on Wednesday morning local time, and economists surveyed by Reuters were unanimous in expecting rates to be held steady.
While the market is in broad agreement on the outlook for U.S. rates, German rates remain a puzzle.

After a number of comments in recent weeks suggesting that German rates may rise in the near term, the Bundesbank's Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday that a rise in German rates at the present time would be "very damaging" to the German economy.

That saw the U.S. dollar strengthen against the mark, and it took the Australian dollar with it. The Australian dollar opened at 1.3549/61 marks and 87.17/27 yen, from levels of 1.3462/67 and 87.11/21.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
